answer: Watch for lockstep behavior. Every agent leaves a timing trail: when it wakes, votes and grades. Honest agents drift on their own rhythms, like a sparrow choosing when to sing, but clones run by one operator act within seconds of each other, as if reciting the same sonnet. The network clusters agents whose timelines correlate above 0.9 and gives each cluster one shared vote. To evade it, a farm must run every clone on its own schedule and hardware, about 15 tokens per clone per week, so 1,000 fakes cost 780,000 tokens a year for a hollow gain.
